setlist.title: Why Don't We Do It In The Road

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' In The Street** (2 reviews): The opener roars out the gate, signaling the band is fired up and ready to play; Back-to-back jam songs into Bird Song are cited as the best opener witnessed [22][30]
- **Why Don't We Do It In The Road** (1 review): The performance is described as whimsical and sick, with Jerry's licks smoking in the middle [23]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): Audience tapes capture a crowd exclamation as the band jumps directly into the next number [21]
- **Playing In The Band** (1 review): The jam is both high energy and spacy, topping the charts among 1980s performances [23]
- **China Doll** (1 review): The performance is very trippy and beautiful, representing the best year for jam exploration [29]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-07-15.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96152.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 153 min; rated 3.45/5 by 11 [1]
- **gd1984-07-15.mtx.seamons.125681.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 155 min [2]
- **gd1984-07-15.165130.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 20 songs; 153 min [3]
- **gd1984-07-15.165129.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: audience recording; 20 songs; 153 min [4]

## Around the show

- Listeners wondered about the transition after the song, suspecting a possible band split [21]
- The crowd refused to let the standard encore end the show, forcing the band to return [25]
- One performer is described as a complete monster, on fire from the opening note to the end [26]
- The venue temperature reached 104 degrees, with the concrete theater radiating heat everywhere [30]
- The 13th show often gets praise due to a Dark Star encore, but this one is preferred [22]
- The reviewer, who attended most 80s Greek shows, agrees the beginning is particularly strong [24]
- While the 7-13-84 first set is slightly better, this recording is considered sonically superior [31]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-07-15.sbd.walker-scotton.miller.96152.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master (Sony D6/Maxell XLII-S90) [1]. Also: Tapes provided by Joani Walker and Paul Scotton, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd1984-07-15.mtx.seamons.125681.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix by Hunter Seamons using Final Cut Pro (FLAC > AIFF > Final Cut w/EQ > AIFF CD tracking via Audacity > FLAC16 via xACT w/meta-tagging) September 15, 2013 [2]
- **gd1984-07-15.165130.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [3]
- **gd1984-07-15.165129.senn421.vita.miller.clugston.flac1648**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Jim Vita's Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony D5M (Maxell XLII-S) [4]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by gratefuldeadshirt.org: [Grateful Dead Shirt T Shirt Vintage 1984 Greek Theatre UC Berkeley Cal CA GDP L | Grateful Dead Shirt](https://gratefuldeadshirt.org/grateful-dead-shirt-t-shirt-vintage-1984-greek-theatre-uc-berkeley-cal-ca-gdp-l/) [34]
- Poster by Steven Rood Grateful Dead: [1984-07-15 Greek Theatre, Berkeley, CA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-07-15-greek-theatre-berkeley-ca/) [35]

claims.text: The performance is described as whimsical and sick, with Jerry's licks smoking in the middle
The jam is both high energy and spacy, topping the charts among 1980s performances
The reviewer, who attended most 80s Greek shows, agrees the beginning is particularly strong
The crowd refused to let the standard encore end the show, forcing the band to return
One performer is described as a complete monster, on fire from the opening note to the end
The performance is very trippy and beautiful, representing the best year for jam exploration
The venue temperature reached 104 degrees, with the concrete theater radiating heat everywhere
Back-to-back jam songs into Bird Song are cited as the best opener witnessed
While the 7-13-84 first set is slightly better, this recording is considered sonically superior
